metadata.name: export
metadata.displayName: export - Set export attribute for variables
metadata.description: Mark shell variables for export to child processes

installation.note: export is a shell built-in (bash, sh, etc.)

overview.summary: export marks shell variables so they are passed to child processes (commands you run from the shell). Without export, a variable is only visible in the current shell. It is commonly used to set PATH, environment variables for programs, or temporary overrides.
when_to_use: Set an environment variable for the current session and children
Add to PATH for the session
Pass variables to scripts or commands you run

syntax.description: export NAME marks NAME for export (keeps current value). export NAME=value sets and exports in one step.

examples.title: Add to PATH
examples.description: Append /usr/local/bin to PATH for this session and child processes
examples.use_case: Use a local binary without full path

examples.title: Set and export a variable
examples.description: Set MYVAR and make it visible to child processes

related_commands.description: Run a command with modified environment; env shows current env
Run script in current shell (variables set there are in current shell)
